text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a split demote model for prefix cache where hot residency and prefetch ownership are separated. thinking this reduces handoff contention but complicates eviction invariants.
aj: Curious, does 'split' mean two independent leases per prefix (resident_lease vs prefetch_lease)? :thinking:
mar ia: yes — resident_lease pins active KV in the slab, prefetch_lease drives background rehydrate. they have different liveness windows and credit accounting.
tom: FWIW we tried dual-lease in spike21 and saw a race where demote path could fire while prefetch was still inflight, leading to a ghost read. need a clear ordering.
maria: exactly — we can avoid ghost reads by making demote require either prefetch_lease==none OR prefetch_epoch <= demote_epoch. But that forces extra epoch checks on critical path. tradeoff: extra checks vs occasional read-repair.
nina: Another idea: make demote a two-phase op: advertise demote_intent, wait short grace window for in-flight prefetches to ack, then complete. adds latency but keeps hot path cheap.
aj: How long is "short"? if 50ms we're fine, but across nodes 50-200ms variability. also we need to reason about bursty prefetches — grace could allow spikes.
maria: Proposal sketch: demote_intent with TTL = config.demote_grace_ms (default 100). prefetch workers must check for active intents and either cancel or backoff and ack. demote completes after TTL or after explicit acks.
sam: Sounds sane. needs ops controls: config flags to toggle for rollout and telemetry to count acks vs timeouts.
maria: minimal config example:
```yaml
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  worker_count: 8
demote:
  grace_ms: 100
  require_ack: false
```
aj: If require_ack=true then we block demote until all acks. might cause cascading delays under overload. default false + metrics seems safer.
tom: Concern: multi-tenant fairness — a tenant can pin prefetches and starve demotes if worker_count isn't proportional. we need admission control or tenant-relative quotas.
nina: Agree. Suggest adding soft quotas per-tenant prefetch_slots and global reservation for demote path to preempt some slots.
maria: Implementation plan: 1) add demote_intent metadata to prefix ledger (small 64-bit) 2) prefetch workers + local caches check intent before writing 3) demote uses TTL + optional ack short-circuit 4) rollout behind feature-flag.
sam: Also add internal metric: demote_intent_acks_total and demote_intent_timeouts_total. Ops alert if timeouts > 1% for 5m.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: github.com/redwood/inference/eng-runtime/prefetch-demote-refactor · CI passed · canary 1/5 nodes scheduled
aj: One more correctness corner: what if demote intent is created then node crash loses intent before demote completes? we must make demote idempotent and safe to re-run.
maria: demote uses epoch-based idempotency key (prefix, demote_epoch, demote_uuid). if intent disappears, new scheduler should consider demote_epoch persisted in ledger; older prefetch writes must be compared against demote_epoch to avoid resurrecting.
tom: Ok. For migration: start with require_ack=false, demote_grace_ms=50, instrument heavy telemetry for 24-48h, then flip require_ack=true in a controlled canary if timeouts are negligible.
nina: Test plan: unit tests for intent set/unset, integration with simulated prefetch delay, chaos test where prefetch worker restarts mid-ack, and perf bench for added epoch checks on read path.
sam: Ops runbook add: if demote_timeouts spike, enable prefetch backoff and roll demote_grace_ms up to 500ms, or flip feature flag off.
maria: I'll open RFC follow-up PR with the sketch and the test matrix. tagging @aj @tom for review. :thumbsup:
